newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks leapt to higher levels in early trading on Tuesday morning, on the back of a large gain in the Wall Street Dow Jones and on hedge funds' need to regain their positions, brokers said.
"The market was oversold last week and many investors are buying back, particularly hedge funds," said David Williamson, institutional sales at UBS Securities (East Asia).

The Hang Seng Index advanced 115 points at the open before easing to trade 60 points up at 11,272.85 after 45 minutes of trade. Turnover was much stronger than recent opening sessions at HK$1.14 billion.
"The market has opened quite nicely but I expect some profit-taking at the 11,400 level," said another broker with a British securities house.
UBS' Williamson also saw resistance at that level and said he expected the index to trend in the 10,900 to 11,400 range until later in the month.
"The market has interest rates on the brain," Williamson said, referring to the U.S. Federal Reserve's FMOC meeting scheduled for September 24.
He said while he does not expect a rise in U.S. rates, he also does not see the Hang Seng rising above its resistance level before the conclusions of the meeting are out.
Property shares led the market up, with the sub-index up 0.80 percent before dropping back. Commercial and industrial issues also saw some buying interest.

Henderson Land rose HK$0.75 to make a new all-time (intra-day) high of HK$62.25, before falling back to HK$62.00. The company will release its earnings results for the full year ended June 30 on Wednesday.
Sun Hung Kai was also up HK$0.75 to trade at HK76.75.
Swire Pacific gained HK$0.50 to HK$68.00. The company is benefitting from the improvement in the property market.
H shares came under some selling pressure. The Hang Seng China Enterprise Index was trading down 0.31 percent.
Red chip Jinhui, which reported a 26.8 percent fall in net profit in first-1996 on Monday, drifted down HK$0.02 to HK$1.24.

CNPC (Hong Kong) declined a mere HK$0.005 to HK$0.36 despite news released Tuesday that the company would place 33 million new shares at HK$0.3114 with a Canadian-based investment company Integrated Assets.
China Overseas continued its sideways march, gaining HK$0.05 to HK$2.50 on moderate volume of 2.57 million shares worth HK$6.85 million.
